A financial hub in Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan, launched on 5 July 2018. It sits on the grounds built for Expo 2017.

Its unusual feature is its own legal system. Inside the centre, business disputes go to a court that applies English common law, with judges largely drawn from Britain, and there is a separate arbitration centre. Modelled on a similar centre in Dubai, the idea was to give foreign investors a court they trust in a country whose own courts they do not.

The centre also hosts a stock exchange, the Astana International Exchange, and offers tax breaks to firms that register there. It is part of a long push by Nursultan Nazarbayev, who moved the capital to Astana in 1997, to make the city a showcase and to draw money into an economy that still leans heavily on oil.
